about.title: Gardena Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall at a grocery store, apartment complex, or restaurant in Gardena can leave you with medical bills and missed work almost overnight. Los Angeles County property owners along corridors like Redondo Beach Boulevard and Normandie Avenue have a legal duty to keep their premises reasonably safe, and California law requires showing they knew or should have known about a hazard and failed to address it. That's often the hardest part of these cases — proving notice before evidence disappears. Surveillance footage from a store or apartment complex may only be kept for a short window, and spills, torn carpet, or broken steps get cleaned up or repaired fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in the Gardena area who can help you document the scene, request video before it's overwritten, and evaluate whether the property owner failed in its duty to you.

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather evidence — like prior complaints or inspection logs — to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from Gardena businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly can make the difference in preserving proof of how the hazard developed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present your case fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Gardena?
items.answer: Generally, California law gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a claim. If the property is owned by a government entity — a city building or park, for example — that deadline is much shorter, so it's worth checking quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though the amount may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help assess how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: I fell at a business near Western Avenue in Gardena. What should I do first?
items.answer: Take photos of the hazard, note the time and location, and ask if the business has surveillance cameras covering the area. Reporting the incident and seeking medical care promptly also helps document what happened before evidence or memories fade.
